sessions.title: Explore npm-hub shell nesting + tunnel (@explore subagent)

info.title: Explore npm-hub shell nesting + tunnel (@explore subagent)

parts.text:
Repo: /home/runner/work/zen-panel/zen-panel/fork (Zen Panel). Thoroughness: very thorough.

I need to understand the "npm hub оболочка → в оболочку → в еще одну оболочку" (shell into shell into another shell) architecture and the connection/tunnel chain, especially how a GitHub Actions runner is reached from the hub.

Investigate and report on:
1. `npm-hub/src/tunnel.js` — full summary: what tunnel providers exist (cloudflare quick tunnel / named tunnel / cloudflared invocation), how the URL is discovered, how failures are handled.
2. `npm-hub/src/server.js` (227KB — grep for relevant parts): how terminals/PTYs are created, how "shell into shell" nesting works, SSH/pty/tmux usage, any host/port config, any bind address (127.0.0.1 vs 0.0.0.0), any docker/ssh/jump-host code, tunnel endpoints registered in the UI.
3. `.github/workflows/hub.yml` (1189 lines) — how the runner starts the hub, what ports it exposes, how it publishes the session state / URL (session-state, publish_session), any cloudflared install & flags, any `--tunnel=` CLI flag usage, any docker usage, any public IP/DNS.
4. `tools/open_tunnel.sh`, `tools/tunnel_keeper.sh`, `tools/tunnel_health.sh`, `tools/publish_session.sh`, `tools/hub_control.sh` — what each does, flags, and how they interact.
5. `npm-hub/CLOUD_PHONE_TODO.md` and `TESTING.md` — summarize known failures F-xx and any notes about connecting by IP, Docker, public DNS, or Cloudflare.
6. Any existing docker/compose files, SSH keys, jump host config, or `~/.ssh/config` handling anywhere in the repo. Search for `docker`, `ProxyJump`, `StrictHostKeyChecking`, `0.0.0.0`, `host.docker.internal`, `trycloudflare`, `cloudflared` across the repo (excluding node_modules, novnc vendor, and other vendored dirs).

Return: a structured report with exact file paths + line numbers for the important parts, the actual commands/flags used, and a clear description of the current connection chain. Do NOT modify any files.

29:   return new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, ms));
30: }
31: 
32: function validPort(port) {
33:   const n = Number(port);
34:   return Number.isInteger(n) && n > 0 && n < 65536 ? n : null;
35: }
36: 
37: function findBin(name) {
38:   try {
39:     execSync(`${IS_WIN ? 'where' : 'which'} ${name}`, { stdio: 'ignore', timeout: 3000 });
40:     return name;
41:   } catch {
42:     return null;
43:   }
44: }
45: 
46: function terminate(proc) {
47:   if (!proc || proc.exitCode !== null || proc.signalCode) return;
48:   try {
49:     if (IS_WIN && proc.pid) {
50:       // cloudflared is sometimes started through cmd.exe on Windows. Killing
51:       // only cmd leaves the connector alive and the next start races it.
52:       execFile('taskkill', ['/pid', String(proc.pid), '/T', '/F'], { windowsHide: true }, () => {});
53:     } else {
54:       proc.kill('SIGTERM');
55:     }
56:   } catch {}
57: }
58: 
59: function error1033(status, body) {
60:   return status === 530 || /\b1033\b|error\s*code\s*:\s*1033/i.test(String(body || ''));
61: }
62: 
63: /**
64:  * Probe the public URL without treating a Cloudflare error page as success.
65:  * 401/403/404 are valid here: they prove that the request reached the local
66:  * application through the tunnel. 5xx and Error 1033 mean the connector is
67:  * not ready (or has gone away).
68:  */
69: function probePublicUrl(url, timeoutMs = CLOUDFLARE_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS, redirects = 0) {
70:   return new Promise(resolve => {
71:     let parsed;
72:     try { parsed = new URL(url); } catch { return resolve({ ok: false, error: 'invalid public URL' }); }
73:     if (!/^https?:$/.test(parsed.protocol)) return resolve({ ok: false, error: 'unsupported public URL' });
74: 
75:     const client = parsed.protocol === 'https:' ? https : http;
76:     const req = client.get(parsed, {
77:       headers: { 'user-agent': 'zen-panel-tunnel-health/1' },
78:       timeout: timeoutMs
79:     }, res => {
80:       let body = '';
81:       res.setEncoding('utf8');
82:       res.on('data', chunk => {
83:         // The body is only used to identify the Cloudflare error page. Do not
84:         // retain an entire HTML response in a long-running hub process.
85:         if (body.length < 65536) body += chunk;
86:       });
87:       res.on('end', () => {
88:         if (res.statusCode >= 300 && res.statusCode < 400 && res.headers.location && redirects < 3) {
89:           const next = new URL(res.headers.location, parsed).toString();
90:           probePublicUrl(next, timeoutMs, redirects + 1).then(resolve);
91:           return;
92:         }
93:         const status = Number(res.statusCode || 0);
94:         resolve({
95:           ok: status >= 200 && status < 500 && !error1033(status, body),
96:           status,
97:           body
98:         });
99:       });
100:     });
101:     req.on('timeout', () => req.destroy(new Error('probe timeout')));
102:     req.on('error', err => resolve({ ok: false, error: err.message }));
103:   });
104: }
105: 
106: async function waitForPublicUrl(url, isAlive, timeoutMs = CLOUDFLARE_READY_TIMEOUT_MS) {
107:   const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
108:   let last = 'edge is still starting';
109:   while (Date.now() < deadline) {
110:     if (typeof isAlive === 'function' && !isAlive()) {
111:       return { ok: false, error: 'cloudflared exited before the edge became ready' };
112:     }
113:     const probe = await probePublicUrl(url);
114:     if (probe.ok) return probe;
115:     last = probe.status ? `HTTP ${probe.status}` : (probe.error || last);
116:     await sleep(2000);
117:   }
118:   return { ok: false, error: `public edge did not become ready (${last})` };
119: }
120: 
121: /**
122:  * Start a child and wait for a URL in either stdout or stderr. The returned
123:  * object also exposes lifecycle hooks so the server can remove a URL as soon
124:  * as the connector exits instead of keeping a dead 1033 link in the UI.
125:  */
126: function spawnTunnel(args, urlRegex, opts = {}) {
127:   const { timeoutMs: requestedTimeout, ...spawnOpts } = opts;
128:   const timeoutMs = Number(requestedTimeout || START_TIMEOUT_MS);
129:   return new Promise(resolve => {
130:     let proc;
131:     try {
132:       proc = spawn(args[0], args.slice(1), {
133:         stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
134:         shell: IS_WIN,
135:         ...spawnOpts
136:       });
137:     } catch (err) {
138:       resolve({ error: `spawn error: ${err.message}` });
139:       return;
140:     }
141: 
142:     let output = '';
143:     let settled = false;
144:     let intentional = false;
145:     let exited = false;
146:     let exitCode = null;
147:     let exitSignal = null;
148:     const exitListeners = [];
149:     let timer;
150: 
151:     const kill = () => terminate(proc);
152:     const fail = message => {
153:       if (settled) return;
154:       settled = true;
155:       clearTimeout(timer);
156:       kill();
157:       resolve({ error: message, output: output.slice(-12000) });
158:     };
159:     const finish = url => {
160:       if (settled) return;
161:       settled = true;
162:       clearTimeout(timer);
163:       const result = {
164:         url,
165:         close: () => {
166:           intentional = true;
167:           kill();
168:         },
169:         onExit: fn => {
170:           if (typeof fn !== 'function') return () => {};
171:           if (exited) setImmediate(() => fn({ code: exitCode, signal: exitSignal, intentional }));
172:           else exitListeners.push(fn);
173:           return () => {
174:             const i = exitListeners.indexOf(fn);
175:             if (i >= 0) exitListeners.splice(i, 1);
176:           };
177:         },
178:         isAlive: () => !exited && proc.exitCode === null && !proc.signalCode,
179:         pid: proc.pid
180:       };
181:       resolve(result);
182:     };
183:     const scan = chunk => {
184:       output = (output + String(chunk)).slice(-120000);
185:       const match = output.match(urlRegex);
186:       if (match && match[1]) finish(match[1]);
187:     };
188: 
189:     timer = setTimeout(() => fail(`timed out waiting for tunnel address (${Math.round(timeoutMs / 1000)}s)`), timeoutMs);
190:     proc.stdout.on('data', scan);
191:     proc.stderr.on('data', scan);
192:     proc.on('error', err => fail(`spawn error: ${err.message}`));
193:     proc.on('exit', (code, signal) => {
194:       exited = true;
195:       exitCode = code;
196:       exitSignal = signal;
197:       if (!settled) {
198:         fail(`tunnel exited before reporting an address (code ${code || 0}${signal ? `, ${signal}` : ''})`);
199:         return;
200:       }
201:       const info = { code, signal, intentional };
202:       for (const fn of exitListeners.splice(0)) {
203:         try { fn(info); } catch {}
204:       }
205:     });
206:   });
207: }
208: 
209: // ─── NGROK ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
210: const NGROK_TOKEN_FILE = path.join(os.homedir(), '.npm-hub-ngrok-token');
211: 
212: function loadNgrokToken() {
213:   try {
214:     if (fs.existsSync(NGROK_TOKEN_FILE)) return fs.readFileSync(NGROK_TOKEN_FILE, 'utf8').trim();
215:   } catch {}
216:   return null;
217: }
218: 
219: function saveNgrokToken(token) {
220:   try {
221:     fs.writeFileSync(NGROK_TOKEN_FILE, token, { mode: 0o600 });
222:     return true;
223:   } catch { return false; }
224: }
225: 
226: async function startNgrok(port) {
227:   const bin = findBin('ngrok');
228:   if (!bin) return { error: 'ngrok not found.\nInstall: https://ngrok.com/download\nOr: choco install ngrok\nOr: scoop install ngrok' };
229: 
230:   const ngrokToken = process.env.NGROK_AUTHTOKEN || loadNgrokToken();
231:   const ngrokArgs = ngrokToken
232:     ? [bin, 'http', String(port), '--log=stdout', `--authtoken=${ngrokToken}`]
233:     : [bin, 'http', String(port), '--log=stdout'];
234:   const result = await spawnTunnel(ngrokArgs, /url=(https:\/\/[^\s]+)/, { timeoutMs: 45000 });
235:   if (result.url) return {
236:     url: result.url, type: 'ngrok', close: result.close,
237:     onExit: result.onExit, isAlive: result.isAlive,
238:     healthCheck: () => probePublicUrl(result.url)
239:   };
240: 
241:   // Some ngrok versions do not print the URL even though their local API is
242:   // available. Preserve that fallback, but still health-check the URL before
243:   // exposing it to the panel.
244:   try {
245:     const apiResult = await new Promise(resolve => {
246:       const req = http.get('http://127.0.0.1:4040/api/tunnels', res => {
247:         let body = '';
248:         res.on('data', d => { if (body.length < 65536) body += d; });
249:         res.on('end', () => {
250:           try { resolve(JSON.parse(body).tunnels?.[0]?.public_url || null); }
251:           catch { resolve(null); }
252:         });
253:       });
254:       req.on('error', () => resolve(null));
255:       req.setTimeout(3000, () => { req.destroy(); resolve(null); });
256:     });
257:     if (apiResult) {
258:       const health = await probePublicUrl(apiResult);
259:       if (health.ok) return {
260:         url: apiResult, type: 'ngrok', close: () => {},
261:         healthCheck: () => probePublicUrl(apiResult)
262:       };
263:     }
264:   } catch {}
265:   return { error: result.error || 'ngrok failed. Check: ngrok http ' + port };
266: }
267: 
268: // ─── LOCALTUNNEL ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
269: async function startLocaltunnel(port) {
270:   const bin = findBin('lt');
271:   if (bin) {
272:     const result = await spawnTunnel([bin, '--port', String(port)], /(https:\/\/[a-zA-Z0-9-]+\.loca\.lt)/, { timeoutMs: 90000 });
273:     if (result.url) return {
274:       url: result.url, type: 'localtunnel', close: result.close,
275:       onExit: result.onExit, isAlive: result.isAlive,
276:       healthCheck: () => probePublicUrl(result.url)
277:     };
278:   }
279: 
280:   const result = await spawnTunnel(['npx', '--yes', 'localtunnel', '--port', String(port)], /(https:\/\/[a-zA-Z0-9-]+\.loca\.lt)/, { timeoutMs: 120000 });
281:   if (result.url) return {
282:     url: result.url, type: 'localtunnel', close: result.close,
283:     onExit: result.onExit, isAlive: result.isAlive,
284:     healthCheck: () => probePublicUrl(result.url)
285:   };
286:   return {
287:     error: `localtunnel failed.\nTry: npm install -g localtunnel\nThen: lt --port ${port}\nOr check internet connection.`
288:   };
289: }
290: 
291: // ─── CLOUDFLARE (cloudflared) ─────────────────────────────────────
292: async function startCloudflare(port) {
293:   const n = validPort(port);
294:   if (!n) return { error: `invalid local port: ${port}` };
295:   const bin = findBin('cloudflared');
296:   if (!bin) return {
297:     error: 'cloudflared not found.\nInstall: https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/connections/connect-networks/downloads/\nOr: choco install cloudflared\nOr: scoop install cloudflared'
298:   };
299: 
300:   // 127.0.0.1 is deliberate. On some Windows hosts localhost resolves to
301:   // ::1 first while the application is listening on IPv4 only; that gives the
302:   // tunnel a healthy process but a dead origin and eventually a 1033/502 page.
303:   const origin = `http://127.0.0.1:${n}`;
304:   const result = await spawnTunnel(
305:     [bin, 'tunnel', '--url', origin, '--no-autoupdate', '--loglevel', 'info'],
306:     /(https:\/\/[a-zA-Z0-9-]+\.trycloudflare\.com)/,
307:     { timeoutMs: START_TIMEOUT_MS }
308:   );
309:   if (!result.url) return { error: result.error || `cloudflared failed. Check: cloudflared tunnel --url ${origin}` };
310: 
311:   // Printing a hostname is not the same as having a connector. Do not expose
312:   // it to the UI/workflow until a real request reaches the local application.
313:   const ready = await waitForPublicUrl(result.url, result.isAlive, CLOUDFLARE_READY_TIMEOUT_MS);
314:   if (!ready.ok) {
315:     result.close();
316:     return {
317:       error: `Cloudflare tunnel did not become reachable: ${ready.error}. ` +
318:         'The old trycloudflare.com address must not be reused (Error 1033).'
319:     };
320:   }
321: 
322:   return {
323:     url: result.url,
324:     type: 'cloudflare',
325:     close: result.close,
326:     onExit: result.onExit,
327:     isAlive: result.isAlive,
328:     healthCheck: () => probePublicUrl(result.url)
329:   };
330: }
331: 
332: // ─── MAIN ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
333: async function startTunnel(port, type) {
334:   switch (type) {
335:     case 'ngrok': return startNgrok(port);
336:     case 'localtunnel': return startLocaltunnel(port);
337:     case 'cloudflare': return startCloudflare(port);
338:     default: return { error: `Unknown tunnel type: ${type}. Use: ngrok | localtunnel | cloudflare` };
339:   }
340: }
341: 
342: module.exports = {
343:   startTunnel,
344:   // Exported for the small regression tests and for the shell launcher to
345:   // share the exact Error 1033 definition.
346:   probePublicUrl,
347:   waitForPublicUrl,
348:   _test: { error1033, validPort }
349: };

# Cloud Phone — доработки и план

## Текущее состояние (коммиты)
- **npm-hub** (репозиторий `zen-panel`):
  - вкладка **Телефон**: кнопки Старт/Стоп/Подключить/⛶, статус, iframe noVNC через `/phone/vnc.html?autoconnect=1&path=ws/vnc`
  - сервер: `/api/phone/status|start|stop`, WS-прокси `/ws/vnc → tcp://127.0.0.1:5900`
  - пульс: sinks `cloud_phone`, `browser_youtube`, loopback'и
  - вкладка **Экран (Linux Desktop)**: параллельный раннер `vnc` в `hub.yml`, который с первой секунды поднимает headless-рабочий стол (openbox + xterm + tint2, Mesa/llvmpipe) на Xvfb :99 и отдаёт его через x11vnc + noVNC + cloudflared-туннель
  - сервер: `/api/vnc/status` читает `session-vnc.json` со ветки `session-state`, `/desktop-vnc` — редирект на живой адрес
- **android-cloud-phone** (origin/main = `5c3c417`):
  - `launch.sh`: Xvfb :99 1080×2400, AVD `phone` (Pixel 7, Android 14, x86_64), KVM, `-no-audio` убран, `QEMU_AUDIO_DRV=alsa`
  - `scripts/control.sh start|stop|status` — управляет стеком (эмулятор, x11vnc, websockify)
  - noVNC встроен в hub (`public/novnc/`)

## Что нужно доделать

### 1. Вкладка «Браузер» — Chrome/Kiwi внутри телефона
- Добавить API `/api/phone/browser` → `adb shell am start -n com.kiwibrowser.browser/com.google.android.apps.chrome.Main -a android.intent.action.VIEW -d <URL>`
- UI: поле ввода URL + кнопка «Открыть», кнопка «▶ YouTube»
- Результат открывается в iframe `/phone/vnc.html` (тот же VNC-стрим, только активность браузера)
- Сохранять последнюю открытую вкладку/историю в localStorage

### 2. Вкладка «Телефон» — стабильность и UX
- Авто-статус при открытии страницы (уже есть)
- Переподключение при разрыве WS (noVNC `reconnect: true`)
- Фуллскрин работает (requestFullscreen)
- Кнопка «Стоп» останавливает телефон через `control.sh stop`

### 3. Эмулятор — где взять и как настроить
**Репозиторий:** `https://github.com/sj0404-collab/android-cloud-phone`
```bash
git clone https://github.com/sj0404-collab/android-cloud-phone
cd android-cloud-phone
./install_deps.sh        # ставит qemu, x11vnc, websockify, tigerVNC, pulseaudio, ffmpeg
# SDK (нужен один раз):
/usr/local/lib/android/sdk/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager "emulator" "platform-tools" "system-images;android-34;default;x86_64"
/usr/local/lib/android/sdk/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/avdmanager create avd -n phone -k "system-images;android-34;default;x86_64" -d pixel_7
# Запуск:
bash scripts/control.sh start
```
**Важно:** `/dev/kvm` должен быть доступен (`sudo chmod 666 /dev/kvm` или добавить пользователя в группу `kvm`). Без KVM эмулятор не запустится.

### 4. Баг: система не откликается на касания, виснет, FPS падает

#### Диагностика (проверить по порядку)
1. **KVM и ускорение**
   - `ls -l /dev/kvm` — должен быть `crw-rw-rw-` и доступен для записи
   - В логе эмулятора (`cloud-phone.log`) искать `KVM acceleration enabled` / `accel: kvm`
   - Если «No KVM access» — эмулятор работает в TCG (медленно, FPS ~1–2)

2. **GPU-бэкенд**
   - Сейчас: `-gpu swiftshader_indirect` (CPU-рендер, низкий FPS)
   - Если на хосте есть GPU — попробовать `-gpu host` (нужен `/dev/dri/renderD128` и mesa)
   - Для headless runner без GPU — `swiftshader_indirect` единственный вариант; FPS 15–30 при 1080×2400

3. **x11vnc — производительность**
   - Флаги в `launch.sh`: `-noxdamage -noprimary -skip_duplicatekeys -shared -forever`
   - Добавить/проверить: `-noxdamage -nodri -noshm -copyrect -quality 6 -compresslevel 6`
   - Отключить композитинг: `-noxdamage` уже есть; `-noshm` иногда помогает на CPU

4. **noVNC — настройки**
   - В `public/novnc/vnc.html` (или при инициализации) можно добавить:
     ```js
     RFB.defaults = { ...RFB.defaults, scaleViewport: true, resizeSession: true };
     ```
   - WS-прокси `/ws/vnc` должен передавать бинарные кадры без перекодирования

5. **Android UI — ANR / System UI диалоги**
   - После загрузки часто появляется ANR `systemui` — диалог «Close app»
   - Авто-закрытие: `adb shell input tap 540 1273` (координаты кнопки «Close app» на 1080×2400)
   - Или `adb shell am force-stop com.android.systemui` (но может сломать лаунчер)

6. **Ресурсы эмулятора**
   - RAM: `-memory 4096` (можно поднять до 6144)
   - CPU cores: `-cores 2` (runner обычно 2–4 vCPU)
   - Отключить снимки/анимации: `-no-snapshot -no-boot-anim` (уже есть)
   - Отключить Vulkan: `-feature -Vulkan` (уже есть)

7. **Сетевой стек / adb**
   - Порт 5554 (adb) — проверка `adb devices`
   - Wi-Fi внутри эмулятора: `AndroidWifi` 10.0.2.0/24, шлюз 10.0.2.2
   - Если интернета нет — `adb shell "settings put global wifi_on 1"` / перезагрузка эмулятора

8. **Аудио (в процессе)**
   - Сейчас `QEMU_AUDIO_DRV=alsa` + `~/.asoundrc` → Pulse sink `cloud_phone`
   - Проверка: `pactl list sink-inputs` — должен появиться клиент `qemu` / `Android` при воспроизведении
   - Если нет — перейти на `-audio pulse` (если QEMU собран с поддержкой pulse) или явный `-audiodev pa`

#### План фиксов (порядок)
1. Проверить KVM (`ls -l /dev/kvm`, лог эмулятора).
2. Запустить `scripts/control.sh start` — дождаться `boot_completed=1`.
3. Запустить x11vnc с расширенными флагами; `websockify 6080 localhost:5900`.
4. Подключиться через hub `/phone/vnc.html` — проверить FPS (glances / `adb shell dumpsys gfxinfo`).
5. Если FPS < 15 — попробовать `-gpu host` (если есть GPU) или снизить разрешение до 720×1520.
6. Добавить авто--dismiss ANR (`adb shell input tap 540 1273` в `wait_for_boot`).
7. Оптимизировать x11vnc: `-noxdamage -nodri -noshm -copyrect`.
8. Аудио: убедиться, что Pulse sink `cloud_phone` получает поток; если нет — переключить на `-audio pulse` (требует QEMU с pulse).

### 5. Полный цикл рестарта (после выключения)
```bash
# 1. Остановить телефон
cd ~/android-cloud-phone && bash scripts/control.sh stop
# 2. Убить остатки
pkill -9 -f "qemu-system|x11vnc|websockify|Xvfb :99"
# 3. Очистить Pulse дубликаты (если hub перезапускался)
pactl list short modules | awk '/null-sink|loopback/ {print $1}' | xargs -r pactl unload-module
# 4. Запустить телефон
tmux new-session -d -s phone "bash launch.sh 2>&1 | tee /tmp/phone.log"
# 5. Ждать boot_completed=1 (1–2 мин)
# 6. Запустить hub (если не жив)
cd /home/runner/work/zen-panel/zen-panel/fork/npm-hub && node src/server.js
# 7. Проверить /api/phone/status → {running:true, adb:true}
# 8. Открыть hub в браузере → вкладка Телефон → «▶ Старт» → «Подключить»
```

### 6. Приоритеты
| # | Задача | Статус |
|---|--------|--------|
| 1 | KVM + GPU ускорение | ✅ KVM работает, GPU — swiftshader |
| 2 | x11vnc флаги для FPS | ✅ добавлены в `launch.sh` (android-cloud-phone) |
| 3 | ANR авто-закрытие | ✅ `dismiss_anr()` в `wait_for_boot` |
| 4 | Аудио в sink `cloud_phone` | 🔄 текущая попытка ALSA→Pulse |
| 5 | Вкладка «Браузер» API + UI | ✅ выполнено + восстановление `cp.lastUrl` |
| 6 | Вкладка «Телефон» — авто-реконнект | ✅ noVNC `reconnect=1` |
| 7 | Документация запуска для CI | ✅ `install_deps.sh`, `control.sh` |
| 8 | Linux Desktop (Экран) — паралл. раннер | ✅ `vnc` job в `hub.yml`, `start_desktop.sh`, кнопка в UI |

---

> **Примечание:** живой hub на порту 8090 (PID 29164) не трогать без нужды — правки вступают в силу после `git push` и следующего рестарта keep-alive workflow.

---

## 0. Текущее состояние (на момент последней правки)

| Область | Состояние |
|---|---|

| `bash -n` по `tools/*.sh` и всем `run:`-шагам | зелёный (проверено вручную, в CI напрямую нет) |
| 11 сьютов в `tests/` (10 js + 1 shell) | зелёные в CI |
| Из них без зависимостей (7 сьютов) | зелёные локально на Windows: 291 проверка, 1 осознанный skip |
| Сборка APK | зелёная: `v1.299`, `hub-v1.299` (коммит `ab63545`) |
| Живой прогон сессии | подтверждён 26.09: запуск → туннель → отмена → слоты `ended` |
| Живой прогон с `HUB_TOKEN` (gate) | **не проверен** — сервер со стартом на gate вживую не запускался |
| Ручные сценарии (VNC, терминалы, файлы, git, mobile) | **не проводились** |

Пробелы покрытия перечислены в §4.

---

## 1. Уровни проверки

| Уровень | Что ловит | Как запустить | Когда |
|---|---|---|---|
| L0 Синтаксис | опечатки в JS/YAML/sh | `JS syntax` (CI) | на каждый push |
| L1 Регрессия UI | логика панелей и хаба без сети | `Tests` (CI) → `tests/npm test` | на каждый push |
| L2 Shell | синтаксис и логика `tools/*.sh` | `bash -n tools/*.sh`, `tests/work-backup-test.sh` | локально перед коммитом |
| L3 Интеграция | живой runner: туннель, PTY, VNC, gate | ручной прогон сессии | после изменения `npm-hub/src` или workflows |
| L4 Приёмка | сценарий целиком на телефоне | ручной чек-лист §3 | перед релизом APK |

---

## 2. Автоматические проверки

### 2.1 Локально

```bash
# регрессия (jsdom; нужен npm ci в tests/)
cd tests && npm ci && npm test

# синтаксис (то же, что делает CI)
for f in tools/*.sh; do bash -n "$f"; done
node --check npm-hub/src/server.js
node --check npm-hub/src/vnc-keepalive.js
node --check npm-hub/src/handoff.js

# проверка YAML всех workflow
python -c "import yaml,glob;[yaml.safe_load(open(f)) for f in glob.glob('.github/workflows/*.yml')]"
```

### 2.2 Сьюиты (`tests/npm test`)

| Сьют | Что ловит | Сеть |
|---|---|---|
| `panel-tabs-e2e.js` | вкладки, слоты, модели, save/stop, 403/429, gate-токены панели | стаб `fetch` |
| `hub-connect-e2e.js` | страница подключения в hub APK: dispatch, опрос сессии, ссылка `/m?zt=` | стаб `fetch` |
| `hub-gate-test.js` | **gate `HUB_TOKEN`**: `?zt=`, заголовок, cookie, loopback, 401 на сокете | без сети, без зависимостей |
| `term-replay-test.js` | **переподключение терминала**: хвост буфера вместо 4 МБ, флаг последнего кадра, сброс терминала, возврат вниз | без сети, без зависимостей |
| `mobile-touch-test.js` | тапы/скролл телефона, дефолтный `hub-work`, плюс grep-инварианты workflows и `tools/` | стаб |
| `handoff-test.js` | конечный автомат handoff на фейковых часах | без сети |
| `opencode-resume-test.js` | отчёт «где я остановился»: id, папки, незакоммиченное | без сети |
| `offline-cache-test.js` | офлайн-слой `offline.js` в `vm`-песочнице | без сети |
| `panel-offline-test.js` | офлайн-слой APK-панели | без сети |
| `vault-test.js` | внешняя память (IndexedDB + SW) | без сети |
| `work-backup-test.sh` | round-trip `backup-work.sh` + `restore-work.sh` на локальном bare-репо | без сети |

### 2.3 Чего в автоматике нет

- `tools/open_tunnel.sh` и `tools/tunnel_health.sh` — **никаких тестов**. Туннель
  и Error 1033 проверяются только L3.
- Клиентская половина терминала (`term-app.js`) покрыта инвариантами исходника,
  а не поведением: `xterm` требует DOM. Настоящая проверка переподключения —
  T-51/T-52 на живом раннере.
- `tools/publish_session.sh` покрыт косвенно (`work-backup-test.sh`), но
  конкурентный пуш двух писателей (слот `linux` против `windows`) — нет.
- APK-сборка проверяется только на GitHub (сборщики), локально не воспроизводится.
- Нет проверки, что gate действительно включён на живом сервере (§4, F-08).

Порядок важен: каждый следующий пункт опирается на предыдущий.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Put a local HTTP port on the public internet with a Cloudflare quick tunnel.
#
# The URL printed by this script is usable only while the cloudflared process
# below is alive. A quick-tunnel hostname may appear in the log before the
# Cloudflare edge has a connector, so this script waits for a real HTTP answer
# and refuses to publish an Error 1033 page.
#
# Usage: open_tunnel.sh <local-port> [log-file]
# Prints one ready https URL on stdout, or nothing and exit 1.

set -uo pipefail

PORT="${1:?usage: open_tunnel.sh <local-port> [log]}"
case "$PORT" in
  ''|*[!0-9]*) echo "open_tunnel: invalid port: $PORT" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac
if [ "$PORT" -lt 1 ] || [ "$PORT" -gt 65535 ]; then
  echo "open_tunnel: invalid port: $PORT" >&2
  exit 1
fi

HUB_LOGS="${HUB_LOGS:-$HOME/.npm-hub/logs}"
HUB_TMP="${HUB_TMP:-$HOME/.npm-hub/tmp}"
mkdir -p "$HUB_LOGS" "$HUB_TMP"
# A second tunnel on the SAME local port (the Z11 reserve address) passes
# TUNNEL_TAG=reserve: it gets its own pid/url/log files and skips the shared
# port-wide pkill, so maintaining the reserve never shoots the main tunnel.
TAG="${TUNNEL_TAG:-}"
LOG="${2:-$HUB_LOGS/cloudflared-$PORT${TAG:+-$TAG}.log}"
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$LOG")" 2>/dev/null || true
PIDFILE="$HUB_LOGS/cloudflared-$PORT${TAG:+-$TAG}.pid"
URLFILE="$HUB_LOGS/cloudflared-$PORT${TAG:+-$TAG}.url"
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

# Kill only the connector for this origin. The bracket in the pattern keeps
# pkill from matching the shell that is executing this script. The pidfile is
# preferred because it cannot accidentally match another tunnel.
kill_old() {
  local old=""
  old="$(cat "$PIDFILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  if [ -n "$old" ] && kill -0 "$old" 2>/dev/null; then
    kill "$old" 2>/dev/null || true
    for _ in 1 2 3 4 5; do
      kill -0 "$old" 2>/dev/null || break
      sleep 1
    done
  fi
  rm -f "$PIDFILE" "$URLFILE"
  if [ -z "$TAG" ]; then
    pkill -f "cloudflared [t]unnel --url http://localhost:$PORT" 2>/dev/null || true
    pkill -f "cloudflared [t]unnel --url http://127[.]0[.]0[.]1:$PORT" 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
}
kill_old

if ! command -v cloudflared >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  download="$HUB_TMP/cloudflared.$$"
  if ! curl -fL --retry 3 --connect-timeout 15 -o "$download" \
      https://github.com/cloudflare/cloudflared/releases/latest/download/cloudflared-linux-amd64; then
    rm -f "$download"
    echo "open_tunnel: cloudflared download failed" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  chmod +x "$download"
  if sudo -n mv "$download" /usr/local/bin/cloudflared 2>/dev/null; then
    :
  else
    mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/bin"
    mv "$download" "$HOME/.local/bin/cloudflared"
    export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
  fi
fi

CF="$(command -v cloudflared 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [ -z "$CF" ] || [ ! -x "$CF" ]; then
  echo "open_tunnel: cloudflared is not executable" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# Use IPv4 explicitly. On some hosts localhost resolves to ::1 while the
# service listens only on IPv4; cloudflared then stays alive with a dead origin.
nohup "$CF" tunnel --url "http://127.0.0.1:$PORT" \
  --no-autoupdate --loglevel info >"$LOG" 2>&1 &
PID=$!
echo "$PID" > "$PIDFILE"

URL=""
# The quick-tunnel hostname normally appears in 10–20 seconds. Keep polling
# for up to 80 seconds, but stop immediately if the connector exits.
for _ in $(seq 1 40); do
  if ! kill -0 "$PID" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "open_tunnel: cloudflared exited before reporting an address" >&2
    tail -30 "$LOG" >&2 2>/dev/null || true
    rm -f "$PIDFILE"
    exit 1
  fi
  URL="$(grep -Eo 'https://[a-zA-Z0-9-]+[.]trycloudflare[.]com' "$LOG" 2>/dev/null | head -1 || true)"
  [ -n "$URL" ] && break
  sleep 2
done

if [ -z "$URL" ]; then
  echo "open_tunnel: no address after 80s" >&2
  tail -30 "$LOG" >&2 2>/dev/null || true
  kill "$PID" 2>/dev/null || true
  rm -f "$PIDFILE"
  exit 1
fi

# The hostname existing in DNS is not enough. Wait until a request reaches the
# origin; this is what prevents publishing the exact URL that shows Error 1033.
READY=0
for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
  if "$SCRIPT_DIR/tunnel_health.sh" "$URL" "/"; then
    READY=1
    break
  fi
  if ! kill -0 "$PID" 2>/dev/null; then break; fi
  sleep 2
done

if [ "$READY" != 1 ]; then
  echo "open_tunnel: Cloudflare edge never became ready (possible Error 1033)" >&2
  tail -30 "$LOG" >&2 2>/dev/null || true
  kill "$PID" 2>/dev/null || true
  rm -f "$PIDFILE" "$URLFILE"
  exit 1
fi

# Consumers/watchdogs can verify which URL belongs to this pid. Write it only
# after the health check and atomically so a concurrent reader never sees a
# half-written hostname.
printf '%s\n' "$URL" > "$URLFILE.tmp.$$"
mv -f "$URLFILE.tmp.$$" "$URLFILE"
printf '%s\n' "$URL"

1: #!/usr/bin/env bash
2: # Dual-tunnel keeper (Z11): one endpoint, TWO public addresses, all the time.
3: #
4: # WHY
5: #   A quick tunnel dies eventually; when it is the only address the user's
6: #   phone instantly shows «Не открывается» until somebody repairs it. With a
7: #   reserve address always warm, the app just walks over to it (see the hub
8: #   APK: url2 fallback) while this daemon resurrects the main one. Repair no
9: #   longer depends on the job's keep-alive step being alive: this loop owns
10: #   both addresses by itself.
11: #
12: # WHAT IT OWNS
13: #   main    the workflow's own address (opened by the job, refreshed by the
14: #           watchdog when that survives - this daemon only fills in when the
15: #           address dropped and stayed dropped for ~a minute)
16: #   reserve TUNNEL_TAG=reserve, its own pid/url/log files, refreshed here on
17: #           every death and republished straight into the session descriptor
18: #
19: # PUBLISHED KEYS (preserved by url2-merge upstream in this workflow)
20: #   hub: url, hubUrl, desktop, mobile + url2 (reserve base)
21: #   vnc: url, novncUrl (+ url /vnc.html) + url2 (reserve base)
22: set -uo pipefail
23: 
24: VM="${1:-hub}"          # hub | vnc
25: HUB_LOGS="${HUB_LOGS:-$HOME/.npm-hub/logs}"
26: mkdir -p "$HUB_LOGS" 2>/dev/null || true
27: TOOLS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
28: TOKEN="${GH_TOKEN:-${GITHUB_TOKEN:-}}"
29: [ -z "$TOKEN" ] && { echo "[tunnel-keeper] no token" >&2; exit 1; }
30: 
31: if [ "$VM" = "vnc" ]; then
32:   PORT=6081; SLOT=vnc; URLFILE="$HUB_LOGS/vnc-url"; HEALTH_PATH="/vnc.html"
33:   R_URLFILE="$HUB_LOGS/vnc-url2"
34: else
35:   PORT=8090; SLOT=hub-linux; URLFILE="$HUB_LOGS/hub-url"; HEALTH_PATH="/"
36:   R_URLFILE="$HUB_LOGS/hub-url2"
37: fi
38: INTERVAL="${KEEPER_INTERVAL:-20}"
39: MAIN_FAILS=0
40: 
41: log() { echo "[tunnel-keeper:$VM $(date -u '+%H:%M:%S')] $*" | tee -a "$HUB_LOGS/tunnel-keeper.log"; }
42: 
43: healthy() {  # $1 = url
44:   [ -n "$1" ] && bash "$TOOLS_DIR/tunnel_health.sh" "$1" "$HEALTH_PATH" >/dev/null 2>&1
45: }
46: 
47: url_for_pidfile() {  # $1 = pidfile path
48:   local p
49:   p="$(tr -dc '0-9' < "$1" 2>/dev/null || true)" || true
50:   [ -n "${p:-}" ] && kill -0 "$p" 2>/dev/null || return 1
51:   cat "${1%.pid}.url" 2>/dev/null || true
52: }
53: 
54: publish_pair() {  # args k=v ... (always includes both base urls we know)
55:   local main reserve
56:   main="$(cat "$URLFILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
57:   reserve="$(cat "$R_URLFILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
58:   if [ "$SLOT" = "hub-linux" ]; then
59:     GH_TOKEN="$TOKEN" bash "$TOOLS_DIR/publish_session.sh" \
60:       "slot=hub-linux" "kind=NPM-Hub" "os=linux" \
61:       ${main:+"url=$main"} ${main:+"hubUrl=$main"} ${main:+"desktop=$main/d"} ${main:+"mobile=$main/m"} \
62:       ${reserve:+"url2=$reserve"} \
63:       "auth=без пароля" "label=${HUB_LABEL:-hub}" 2>&1 | tail -1
64:   else
65:     GH_TOKEN="$TOKEN" bash "$TOOLS_DIR/publish_session.sh" \
66:       "slot=vnc" "kind=Linux-VNC" "os=linux" \
67:       ${main:+"url=$main/vnc.html"} ${main:+"novncUrl=$main/vnc.html"} \
68:       ${reserve:+"url2=$reserve"} \
69:       "label=${HUB_LABEL:-hub}" 2>&1 | tail -1
70:   fi
71: }
72: 
73: open_reserve() {
74:   local url
75:   url="$(TUNNEL_TAG=reserve bash "$TOOLS_DIR/open_tunnel.sh" "$PORT" "$HUB_LOGS/tunnel-reserve.log" 2>/dev/null || echo)"
76:   if [ -n "$url" ]; then
77:     echo "$url" > "$R_URLFILE"
78:     log "reserve tunnel up: $url"
79:   else
80:     log "reserve tunnel reopen failed (retry next loop)"
81:   fi
82: }
83: 
84: open_main() {
85:   local url
86:   url="$(bash "$TOOLS_DIR/open_tunnel.sh" "$PORT" "$HUB_LOGS/keeper-tunnel.log" 2>/dev/null || echo)"
87:   if [ -n "$url" ]; then
88:     echo "$url" > "$URLFILE"
89:     log "main tunnel resurrected: $url (the keep-alive step was not up to it)"
90:   else
91:     log "main tunnel reopen failed (retry next loop)"
92:   fi
93: }

# Dual-tunnel keeper (Z11): one endpoint, TWO public addresses, all the time.
#
# WHY
#   A quick tunnel dies eventually; when it is the only address the user's
#   phone instantly shows «Не открывается» until somebody repairs it. With a

#           watchdog when that survives - this daemon only fills in when the
#           address dropped and stayed dropped for ~a minute)
#   reserve TUNNEL_TAG=reserve, its own pid/url/log files, refreshed here on

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Dual-tunnel keeper (Z11): one endpoint, TWO public addresses, all the time.
#
# WHY
#   A quick tunnel dies eventually; when it is the only address the user's
#   phone instantly shows «Не открывается» until somebody repairs it. With a
#   reserve address always warm, the app just walks over to it (see the hub
#   APK: url2 fallback) while this daemon resurrects the main one. Repair no
#   longer depends on the job's keep-alive step being alive: this loop owns
#   both addresses by itself.
#
# WHAT IT OWNS
#   main    the workflow's own address (opened by the job, refreshed by the
#           watchdog when that survives - this daemon only fills in when the
#           address dropped and stayed dropped for ~a minute)
#   reserve TUNNEL_TAG=reserve, its own pid/url/log files, refreshed here on
#           every death and republished straight into the session descriptor
#
# PUBLISHED KEYS (preserved by url2-merge upstream in this workflow)
#   hub: url, hubUrl, desktop, mobile + url2 (reserve base)
#   vnc: url, novncUrl (+ url /vnc.html) + url2 (reserve base)
set -uo pipefail

VM="${1:-hub}"          # hub | vnc
HUB_LOGS="${HUB_LOGS:-$HOME/.npm-hub/logs}"
mkdir -p "$HUB_LOGS" 2>/dev/null || true
TOOLS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
TOKEN="${GH_TOKEN:-${GITHUB_TOKEN:-}}"
[ -z "$TOKEN" ] && { echo "[tunnel-keeper] no token" >&2; exit 1; }

if [ "$VM" = "vnc" ]; then
  PORT=6081; SLOT=vnc; URLFILE="$HUB_LOGS/vnc-url"; HEALTH_PATH="/vnc.html"
  R_URLFILE="$HUB_LOGS/vnc-url2"
else
  PORT=8090; SLOT=hub-linux; URLFILE="$HUB_LOGS/hub-url"; HEALTH_PATH="/"
  R_URLFILE="$HUB_LOGS/hub-url2"
fi
INTERVAL="${KEEPER_INTERVAL:-20}"
MAIN_FAILS=0

log() { echo "[tunnel-keeper:$VM $(date -u '+%H:%M:%S')] $*" | tee -a "$HUB_LOGS/tunnel-keeper.log"; }

healthy() {  # $1 = url
  [ -n "$1" ] && bash "$TOOLS_DIR/tunnel_health.sh" "$1" "$HEALTH_PATH" >/dev/null 2>&1
}

url_for_pidfile() {  # $1 = pidfile path
  local p
  p="$(tr -dc '0-9' < "$1" 2>/dev/null || true)" || true
  [ -n "${p:-}" ] && kill -0 "$p" 2>/dev/null || return 1
  cat "${1%.pid}.url" 2>/dev/null || true
}

publish_pair() {  # args k=v ... (always includes both base urls we know)
  local main reserve
  main="$(cat "$URLFILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  reserve="$(cat "$R_URLFILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  if [ "$SLOT" = "hub-linux" ]; then
    GH_TOKEN="$TOKEN" bash "$TOOLS_DIR/publish_session.sh" \
      "slot=hub-linux" "kind=NPM-Hub" "os=linux" \
      ${main:+"url=$main"} ${main:+"hubUrl=$main"} ${main:+"desktop=$main/d"} ${main:+"mobile=$main/m"} \
      ${reserve:+"url2=$reserve"} \
      "auth=без пароля" "label=${HUB_LABEL:-hub}" 2>&1 | tail -1
  else
    GH_TOKEN="$TOKEN" bash "$TOOLS_DIR/publish_session.sh" \
      "slot=vnc" "kind=Linux-VNC" "os=linux" \
      ${main:+"url=$main/vnc.html"} ${main:+"novncUrl=$main/vnc.html"} \
      ${reserve:+"url2=$reserve"} \
      "label=${HUB_LABEL:-hub}" 2>&1 | tail -1
  fi
}

open_reserve() {
  local url
  url="$(TUNNEL_TAG=reserve bash "$TOOLS_DIR/open_tunnel.sh" "$PORT" "$HUB_LOGS/tunnel-reserve.log" 2>/dev/null || echo)"
  if [ -n "$url" ]; then
    echo "$url" > "$R_URLFILE"
    log "reserve tunnel up: $url"
  else
    log "reserve tunnel reopen failed (retry next loop)"
  fi
}

open_main() {
  local url
  url="$(bash "$TOOLS_DIR/open_tunnel.sh" "$PORT" "$HUB_LOGS/keeper-tunnel.log" 2>/dev/null || echo)"
  if [ -n "$url" ]; then
    echo "$url" > "$URLFILE"
    log "main tunnel resurrected: $url (the keep-alive step was not up to it)"
  else
    log "main tunnel reopen failed (retry next loop)"
  fi
}

trap 'log "stopped"; exit 0' TERM INT
log "keeper up ($VM, port $PORT; reserve pid via TUNNEL_TAG=reserve)"
while true; do
  sleep "$INTERVAL"
  # ── reserve ──
  r_pid_ok=0; r_url="$(url_for_pidfile "$HUB_LOGS/cloudflared-$PORT-reserve.pid" || true)"
  [ -n "${r_url:-}" ] && healthy "$r_url" && r_pid_ok=1
  if [ "$r_pid_ok" = "0" ]; then
    open_reserve
    r_url="$(cat "$R_URLFILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    publish_pair || true
  fi
  # ── main (only kick it after several consecutive dead probes: a busy CPU
  # can make a single probe time out, same rule as the job watchdog) ──
  m_pid_ok=0; m_url="$(url_for_pidfile "$HUB_LOGS/cloudflared-$PORT.pid" || true)"
  if [ -n "${m_url:-}" ] && healthy "$m_url"; then
    [ "${m_url:-}" != "$(cat "$URLFILE" 2>/dev/null)" ] && echo "$m_url" > "$URLFILE" || true
    MAIN_FAILS=0
  else
    MAIN_FAILS=$((MAIN_FAILS + 1))
  fi
  if [ "$MAIN_FAILS" -ge 3 ]; then
    log "main tunnel dead $MAIN_FAILS probes in a row; reserve keeps serving - reopening main"
    open_main
    publish_pair || true
    MAIN_FAILS=0
  fi
done

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Return success only when a public tunnel reaches the local service.
# Cloudflare can resolve a quick-tunnel hostname before a connector is ready;
# that page is HTTP 530 / Error 1033 and must not be treated as healthy.
set -uo pipefail

URL="${1:?usage: tunnel_health.sh <url> [path]}"
PATH_SUFFIX="${2:-/}"
case "$PATH_SUFFIX" in
  /*) ;;
  *) PATH_SUFFIX="/$PATH_SUFFIX" ;;
esac

TMP_DIR="${HUB_TMP:-${HOME:-/tmp}/.npm-hub/tmp}"
mkdir -p "$TMP_DIR" 2>/dev/null || TMP_DIR="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}"
BODY="$TMP_DIR/tunnel-probe.$$"
trap 'rm -f "$BODY"' EXIT

code=$(curl -sS -L --max-time "${TUNNEL_PROBE_TIMEOUT:-15}" \
  -A 'zen-panel-tunnel-health/1' -o "$BODY" -w '%{http_code}' \
  "${URL%/}${PATH_SUFFIX}" 2>/dev/null || true)

# A 401/403/404 proves that the request crossed the tunnel and reached the
# application. A 5xx, or a page mentioning 1033, means the connector is dead.
if grep -Eqi '(^|[^0-9])1033([^0-9]|$)|error[[:space:]]*code[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*1033' "$BODY" 2>/dev/null; then
  exit 1
fi
case "$code" in
  2*|3*|4*) exit 0 ;;
  *) exit 1 ;;
esac

1: #!/usr/bin/env bash
2: # Remote-control + heartbeat daemon for one runner VM (Z10 round 2).
3: #

6: #   assumption: the workflow starts TWO VMs (hub web + VNC desktop) and the
7: #   hub VM's agent itself can die, taking every step with it while detached
8: #   daemons keep breathing. So now:
9: #     - BOTH VMs run this daemon, each with its own CONTROL_TARGET
10: #     - liveness is verifiable from outside: control/heartbeat-<vm>.json is
11: #       rewritten every 2 minutes with a process census
12: #     - this daemon can REPAIR, not only report: reopen-tunnel and up-hub fix
13: #       the exact failure mode of a dead cloudflared / dead hub server without
14: #       needing the job's keep-alive step at all
15: #
16: # CHANNEL (session-state branch)
17: #   control/queue.json             one slot: { seq, op, target?, from? }
18: #                                  target = hub | vnc | any (default any)
19: #   control/results/<seq>-<vm>.json per-VM ack
20: #   control/heartbeat-<vm>.json    liveness + process census every 2 min
21: #
22: # WHITELIST (never arbitrary shell)
23: #   ping, backup-now, handoff-save, restart-hub, up-hub, reopen-tunnel
24: set -uo pipefail
25:

30: 
31: TOKEN="${GH_TOKEN:-${GITHUB_TOKEN:-}}"
32: if [ -z "$TOKEN" ]; then
33:   log "no token - the command queue stays cold"
34:   exit 1
35: fi
36: REPO="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:-sj0404-collab/zen-panel}"
37: BRANCH="${CONTROL_BRANCH:-session-state}"
38: INTERVAL="${CONTROL_INTERVAL:-20}"
39: HEARTBEAT_SEC="${CONTROL_HEARTBEAT_SEC:-120}"
40: API="https://api.github.com/repos/$REPO/contents"
41: QUEUE_PATH="control/queue.json"
42: SEEN_FILE="$HUB_LOGS/hub-control-$VM.seen"
43: SEEN="$(cat "$SEEN_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
44: TOOLS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
45: HUB_PORT="${HUB_PORT:-8090}"

47: trap 'log "stopped"; exit 0' TERM INT
48:

50:   local body
51:   body="$(curl -sf -m 20 -H "Authorization: token $TOKEN" "$API/$1?ref=$BRANCH" 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
52:   echo "$body"
53: }
54: 
55: api_put() {
56:   local b64 sha
57:   b64="$(printf '%s' "$2" | base64 -w0)"

60:     curl -sf -m 25 -X PUT -H "Authorization: token $TOKEN" "$API/$1" \
61:       -d "{\"message\":\"control: ack $1\",\"content\":\"$b64\",\"branch\":\"$BRANCH\",\"sha\":\"$sha\"}" >/dev/null
62:   else
63:     curl -sf -m 25 -X PUT -H "Authorization: token $TOKEN" "$API/$1" \
64:       -d "{\"message\":\"control: ack $1\",\"content\":\"$b64\",\"branch\":\"$BRANCH\"}" >/dev/null
65:   fi
66: }
67: 
68: publish_url() {  # $1 = slot, $2 = new tunnel base url (no trailing slash)
69:   local slot="$1" base="$2" rv
70:   if [ "$slot" = "hub-linux" ]; then
71:     rv="$(cat "$HUB_LOGS/hub-url2" 2>/dev/null || true)"

137:     *)
138:       echo "unknown op: $1" >&2

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Remote-control + heartbeat daemon for one runner VM (Z10 round 2).
#
# WHY ROUND 2
#   Round 1 proved the queue works, but run 175 showed it lives on the wrong
#   assumption: the workflow starts TWO VMs (hub web + VNC desktop) and the
#   hub VM's agent itself can die, taking every step with it while detached
#   daemons keep breathing. So now:
#     - BOTH VMs run this daemon, each with its own CONTROL_TARGET
#     - liveness is verifiable from outside: control/heartbeat-<vm>.json is
#       rewritten every 2 minutes with a process census
#     - this daemon can REPAIR, not only report: reopen-tunnel and up-hub fix
#       the exact failure mode of a dead cloudflared / dead hub server without
#       needing the job's keep-alive step at all
#
# CHANNEL (session-state branch)
#   control/queue.json             one slot: { seq, op, target?, from? }
#                                  target = hub | vnc | any (default any)
#   control/results/<seq>-<vm>.json per-VM ack
#   control/heartbeat-<vm>.json    liveness + process census every 2 min
#
# WHITELIST (never arbitrary shell)
#   ping, backup-now, handoff-save, restart-hub, up-hub, reopen-tunnel
set -uo pipefail

HUB_LOGS="${HUB_LOGS:-$HOME/.npm-hub/logs}"
mkdir -p "$HUB_LOGS" 2>/dev/null || true
VM="${CONTROL_TARGET:-hub}"
log() { echo "[hub-control:$VM $(date -u '+%H:%M:%S')] $*" | tee -a "$HUB_LOGS/hub-control-$VM.log"; }

TOKEN="${GH_TOKEN:-${GITHUB_TOKEN:-}}"
if [ -z "$TOKEN" ]; then
  log "no token - the command queue stays cold"
  exit 1
fi
REPO="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:-sj0404-collab/zen-panel}"
BRANCH="${CONTROL_BRANCH:-session-state}"
INTERVAL="${CONTROL_INTERVAL:-20}"
HEARTBEAT_SEC="${CONTROL_HEARTBEAT_SEC:-120}"
API="https://api.github.com/repos/$REPO/contents"
QUEUE_PATH="control/queue.json"
SEEN_FILE="$HUB_LOGS/hub-control-$VM.seen"
SEEN="$(cat "$SEEN_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
TOOLS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
HUB_PORT="${HUB_PORT:-8090}"

trap 'log "stopped"; exit 0' TERM INT

api_get() {
  local body
  body="$(curl -sf -m 20 -H "Authorization: token $TOKEN" "$API/$1?ref=$BRANCH" 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
  echo "$body"
}

api_put() {
  local b64 sha
  b64="$(printf '%s' "$2" | base64 -w0)"
  sha="$(api_get "$1" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin).get("sha",""))' 2>/dev/null || echo)"
  if [ -n "$sha" ]; then
    curl -sf -m 25 -X PUT -H "Authorization: token $TOKEN" "$API/$1" \
      -d "{\"message\":\"control: ack $1\",\"content\":\"$b64\",\"branch\":\"$BRANCH\",\"sha\":\"$sha\"}" >/dev/null
  else
    curl -sf -m 25 -X PUT -H "Authorization: token $TOKEN" "$API/$1" \
      -d "{\"message\":\"control: ack $1\",\"content\":\"$b64\",\"branch\":\"$BRANCH\"}" >/dev/null
  fi
}

publish_url() {  # $1 = slot, $2 = new tunnel base url (no trailing slash)
  local slot="$1" base="$2" rv
  if [ "$slot" = "hub-linux" ]; then
    rv="$(cat "$HUB_LOGS/hub-url2" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    GH_TOKEN="$TOKEN" bash "$TOOLS_DIR/publish_session.sh" \
      "slot=hub-linux" "kind=NPM-Hub" "os=linux" \
      "url=$base" "hubUrl=$base" "desktop=$base/d" "mobile=$base/m" \
      ${rv:+"url2=$rv"} \
      "auth=без пароля" "label=${HUB_LABEL:-hub}" 2>&1 | tail -1
  else
    rv="$(cat "$HUB_LOGS/vnc-url2" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    GH_TOKEN="$TOKEN" bash "$TOOLS_DIR/publish_session.sh" \
      "slot=vnc" "kind=Linux-VNC" "os=linux" \
      "url=$base/vnc.html" "novncUrl=$base/vnc.html" \
      ${rv:+"url2=$rv"} \
      "label=${HUB_LABEL:-hub}" 2>&1 | tail -1
  fi
}

run_op() {
  local pid url
  case "$1" in
    ping)
      echo "pong from $VM $(date -Iseconds)"
      ;;
    backup-now)
      GH_TOKEN="$TOKEN" GITHUB_TOKEN="$TOKEN" WORK_BACKUP_ROOT="$HOME" \
        bash "$TOOLS_DIR/backup-work.sh" --once
      ;;
    restart-hub)
      pid="$(tr -dc '0-9' < "$HUB_LOGS/hub.pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
      if [ -n "${pid:-}" ] && kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
        kill "$pid" && echo "hub pid $pid signalled"
      else
        echo "no live hub pid (already down?)"
      fi
      ;;
    up-hub)
      if [ "$VM" != "hub" ]; then echo "the npm-hub server lives on the hub VM not $VM"; return 0; fi
      pid="$(tr -dc '0-9' < "$HUB_LOGS/hub.pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
      [ -n "${pid:-}" ] && kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null && { echo "hub already running (pid $pid)"; return 0; }
      (
        cd "$TOOLS_DIR/../npm-hub" || exit 1
        HUB_PORT_STRICT=1 HUB_TOKEN="${HUB_TOKEN_VALUE:-}" HUB_LABEL="${HUB_LABEL:-hub}" \
          GH_TOKEN="$TOKEN" PORT="$HUB_PORT" \
          SESSION_STARTED_MS="$(cat "$HOME/.npm-hub/session-start" 2>/dev/null || date +%s000)" \
          SESSION_LIMIT_MS=21600000 nohup node src/server.js >> "$HUB_LOGS/hub.log" 2>&1 &
        echo $! > "$HUB_LOGS/hub.pid"
      )
      sleep 2; echo "hub relaunched (pid $(cat "$HUB_LOGS/hub.pid" 2>/dev/null))"
      ;;
    reopen-tunnel)
      local port slot
      if [ "$VM" = "hub" ]; then port=8090; slot=hub-linux; else port=6081; slot=vnc; fi
      pid="$(tr -dc '0-9' < "$HUB_LOGS/cloudflared-$port.pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
      [ -n "${pid:-}" ] && kill "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
      pkill -f "cloudflared [t]unnel --url http://127.0.0.1:$port" 2>/dev/null || true
      sleep 1
      url="$(bash "$TOOLS_DIR/open_tunnel.sh" "$port" "$HUB_LOGS/control-tunnel.log" 2>/dev/null || echo)"
      if [ -z "$url" ]; then echo "open_tunnel gave no URL"; return 1; fi
      [ "$VM" = "hub" ] && echo "$url" > "$HUB_LOGS/hub-url" || echo "$url" > "$HUB_LOGS/vnc-url"
      echo "tunnel up: $url"
      publish_url "$slot" "$url"
      ;;
    handoff-save)
      [ "$VM" = "hub" ] || { echo "handoff-save runs on the hub VM"; return 0; }
      GH_TOKEN="$TOKEN" GITHUB_TOKEN="$TOKEN" WORK_BACKUP_ROOT="$HOME" \
        bash "$TOOLS_DIR/handoff.sh"
      ;;
    *)
      echo "unknown op: $1" >&2
      return 64
      ;;
  esac
}

heartbeat() {
  local hb
  hb="$(python3 - <<PYH 2>/dev/null || echo ""
import json, subprocess, datetime
def pc(pat):
    try:
        return subprocess.run(["pgrep","-fc",pat], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10).stdout.strip()
    except Exception:
        return "?"
print(json.dumps({
    "vm": "$VM", "runId": "${GITHUB_RUN_ID:-local}",
    "at": datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"),
    "procs": {
        "hub_server": pc("node src/server.js"),
        "cloudflared": pc("cloudflared [t]unnel"),
        "backup_daemon": pc("[b]ackup-work.sh"),
        "snapshot_daemon": pc("[s]napshot-audit-code.sh"),
        "control_daemon": pc("[h]ub_control.sh"),
        "rescue_ssh": pc("[r]escue_ssh.sh"),
        "tunnel_keeper": pc("[t]unnel_keeper.sh"),
    },
}, ensure_ascii=False))
PYH
)"
  [ -n "$hb" ] && api_put "control/heartbeat-$VM.json" "$hb" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
}

log "queue daemon up ($VM) on $BRANCH:$QUEUE_PATH (every ${INTERVAL}s; seen=$SEEN)"
boot_slot="$(api_get "$QUEUE_PATH" || true)"
if [ -n "$boot_slot" ]; then
  boot_seq="$(python3 -c 'import json,sys,base64; print(json.loads(base64.b64decode(json.load(sys.stdin)["content"])).get("seq",0))' <<<"$boot_slot" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
  if [[ "$boot_seq" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [ "$boot_seq" -gt "$SEEN" ] 2>/dev/null; then
    SEEN="$boot_seq"; echo "$SEEN" > "$SEEN_FILE"
    log "queue baseline set to #$SEEN (stale command - not executing)"
  fi
fi
heartbeat
LAST_BEAT=$SECONDS
while true; do
  sleep "$INTERVAL"
  if [ $((SECONDS - LAST_BEAT)) -ge "$HEARTBEAT_SEC" ]; then
    heartbeat; LAST_BEAT=$SECONDS
  fi
  slot="$(api_get "$QUEUE_PATH" || true)"
  [ -n "$slot" ] || continue
  read -r seq op target < <(python3 -c '
import json, sys
try:
    d = json.loads(sys.stdin.read())
    print(int(d.get("seq", 0)), str(d.get("op", ""))[:64], str(d.get("target", "any"))[:16])
except Exception:
    print(0, "", "any")
' <<<"$(python3 -c 'import json,sys,base64; c=json.load(sys.stdin)["content"]; print(base64.b64decode(c).decode(), end="")' <<<"$slot" 2>/dev/null)" 2>/dev/null || echo "0  any")
  [[ "$seq" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || continue
  [ "$seq" -le "$SEEN" ] 2>/dev/null && continue
  [ -n "$op" ] || continue
  { [ "$target" = "any" ] || [ "$target" = "$VM" ]; } || { log "skip #$seq ($op for target=$target)"; echo "$seq" > "$SEEN_FILE"; SEEN="$seq"; continue; }
  log "command #$seq: $op (target=$target)"
  out="$(run_op "$op" 2>&1 | tail -c 3000)"; rc=$?
  log "command #$seq rc=$rc"
  ack="$(python3 -c '
import json, sys, datetime
print(json.dumps({
    "seq": int(sys.argv[1]), "op": sys.argv[2], "vm": sys.argv[4],
    "ok": sys.argv[3] == "0", "rc": int(sys.argv[3]),
    "at": datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"),
    "runId": sys.argv[5],
    "out": sys.stdin.read()[-2800:],
}, ensure_ascii=False))
' "$seq" "$op" "$rc" "$VM" "${GITHUB_RUN_ID:-local}" <<<"$out" 2>/dev/null || echo "{\"seq\":$seq,\"ok\":false}")"
  if api_put "control/results/$seq-$VM.json" "$ack"; then
    echo "$seq" > "$SEEN_FILE"; SEEN="$seq"
  else
    log "ack push failed - the command WILL rerun until pushed"
  fi
done

1: #!/usr/bin/env bash
2: # Publish the live session's connection details so the panel can show them.
3: #
4: # The job summary already prints the address, user and password, but it is
5: # prose meant for a human with a browser: not machine-readable, and on a phone
6: # it is several taps behind the Actions UI. The panel is where the session is
7: # started, so it is where the credentials belong.
8: #
9: # They go to an orphan branch, session-state, as session.json. An orphan branch
10: # keeps this churn out of the history of main and lets the file be replaced
11: # wholesale every time without ever conflicting.
12: #
13: # WHO CAN READ THIS
14: #   On a public repository the branch is public, and so is the password in it.
15: #   That is the same exposure as the run summary, which is also public - but it
16: #   is worth being explicit, because a password on a web page feels different
17: #   from one in a log. Everything here dies with the runner within six hours,
18: #   and any secret in it is regenerated per run. If that is not acceptable,
19: #   make the repository private; the panel reads it with the same token either
20: #   way.
21: #
22: # TWO DESKS AT ONCE
23: #   Pass slot=linux, slot=windows or slot=agent and the entry lands in its own
24: #   file - session-linux.json, session-windows.json, session-agent.json,
25: #   session-opencode.json and session-hub.json - so
26: #   agent/opencode/hub take an -linux/-windows suffix (one file per OS, so two
27: #   runners stop overwriting each other); the bare slot stays for old runs.
28: #   the two desks and the agent never overwrite each other. Without a slot the
29: #   old single session.json is used, which keeps the older workflows working
30: #   unchanged.
31: #
32: #   The panel reads all three and shows whichever are live.
33: #
34: # MODELS AND SAVED SNAPSHOTS
35: #   Sessions alone do not survive usefully: which model answered, which died,
36: #   which recovered - that roster lives in ~/.zen_free_models.json on the
37: #   runner and dies with it. So every session also publishes its models:
38: #
39: #     publish_session.sh slot=agent file=models-agent.json \
40: #       kind=CLI-агент json=$HOME/.zen_free_models.json
41: #   file= overrides the target on the branch (validated: only the known
42: #   mailboxes are accepted, so a typo cannot spray files across the branch).
43: #   json= merges a local JSON file into the payload - with secrets scrubbed:
44: #   any key looking like a key/token/secret/password is dropped, because
45: #   opencode.json holds API keys and this branch may be public. Pass scrub=0
46: #   to disable.
47: #
48: # LAYOUT OF THE BRANCH (it used to be one pile in the root)
49: #   live/session-<slot>.json      the live descriptor, one per slot
50: #   live/handoff.json             the relay limits + the relay's live status
51: #   models/models-<slot>.json     the model roster of that session
52: #   snapshots/audit.json          the audit trail (was audit.json)
53: #   snapshots/code.json           the code snapshot (was code.json)
54: #   chats/<repo>.json             OpenCode chat bundles (unchanged)
55: #   history/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<Wd>/    everything historical, by day and weekday:
56: #       run-<runNumber>.json         one record per run: success or failure
57: #       saved-<slot>-<stamp>.json    the «Сохранить» snapshots
58: #       audit-<slot>-<stamp>.json
59: #       opencode-<stamp>.json
60: #   artifacts/<file>              files the user pushed from the hub
61: #   Every reader tries the new path first and falls back to the old root name,
62: #   so a branch that was never migrated keeps working.
63: #
64: #   publish_session.sh journal=1 writes the run record:
65: #     publish_session.sh journal=1 slot=hub-linux conclusion=success \
66: #       startedAt=... endedAt=...
67: #
68: # Usage: publish_session.sh key=value ...
69: #   Recognised keys are passed straight through to JSON, so a new session type
70: #   can add a field without touching this script.
71: 
72: set -uo pipefail
73: 
74: BRANCH="session-state"
75: FILE="live/session.json"
76: JOURNAL=0
77: # journal_date can come as an argument or from the environment; without it the
78: # record is filed under today (UTC).
79: JOURNAL_DATE="${JOURNAL_DATE:-}"
80: 
81: # A slot is a routing instruction, not data: pull it out of the arguments
82: # before they become JSON.
83: ARGS=()
84: JSON_FILES=()
85: FILE_OVERRIDE=""
86: SCRUB=1
87: EXPLICIT_STARTED_AT=0
88: for arg in "$@"; do
89:   case "$arg" in
90:     startedAt=*)   EXPLICIT_STARTED_AT=1; ARGS+=("$arg") ;;
91:     journal_date=*) JOURNAL_DATE="${arg#journal_date=}" ;;
92:     slot=linux)    FILE="live/session-linux.json" ;;
93:     slot=windows)  FILE="live/session-windows.json" ;;
94:     slot=agent)    FILE="live/session-agent.json" ;;
95:     slot=agent-linux)    FILE="live/session-agent-linux.json" ;;
96:     slot=agent-windows)  FILE="live/session-agent-windows.json" ;;
97:     slot=opencode) FILE="live/session-opencode.json" ;;
98:     slot=opencode-linux) FILE="live/session-opencode-linux.json" ;;
99:     slot=opencode-windows) FILE="live/session-opencode-windows.json" ;;
100:     slot=hub)      FILE="live/session-hub.json" ;;
101:     slot=hub-linux)      FILE="live/session-hub-linux.json" ;;
102:     slot=hub-windows)    FILE="live/session-hub-windows.json" ;;
103:     slot=phone)    FILE="live/session-phone.json" ;;
104:     slot=vnc)      FILE="live/session-vnc.json" ;;
105:     slot=*)        ;;   # unknown slot: ignore rather than write a stray file
106:     file=*)        FILE_OVERRIDE="$arg" ;;
107:     journal=1)     JOURNAL=1 ;;
108:     scrub=0)       SCRUB=0 ;;
109:     json=*)        # A Windows path (C:\Users\..) breaks mingw python; slashes
110:                    # work for both Windows and mingw python, so normalise.
111:                    _jv="${arg#json=}"; _jv="${_jv//\\//}"; JSON_FILES+=("$_jv") ;;
112:     *)            ARGS+=("$arg") ;;
113:   esac
114: done
115: set -- ${ARGS+"${ARGS[@]}"}
116: 
117: # A file= override that is not one of the known names is refused outright -
118: # the branch is a fixed set of mailboxes, not a scratch disk. The caller keeps
119: # using the old flat names; the layout below turns them into the new folders.
120: if [ -n "$FILE_OVERRIDE" ]; then
121:   _f="${FILE_OVERRIDE#file=}"
122:   if [[ "$_f" =~ ^models-(linux|windows|agent(-linux|-windows)?|opencode(-linux|-windows)?|hub(-linux|-windows)?)\.json$ ]] || \
123:      [[ "$_f" =~ ^(audit|code)\.json$ ]] || \
124:      [[ "$_f" =~ ^chats/[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,80}\.json$ ]] || \
125:      [[ "$_f" =~ ^saved/(audit|code)(-[a-z0-9-]+)?-[0-9]{8}T[0-9]{6}\.json$ ]] || \
126:      [[ "$_f" =~ ^saved/opencode-[0-9]{8}T[0-9]{6}\.json$ ]] || \
127:      [[ "$_f" =~ ^saved/(linux|windows|agent(-linux|-windows)?|opencode(-linux|-windows)?|hub(-linux|-windows)?)-[0-9]{8}T[0-9]{6}\.json$ ]] || \
128:      [[ "$_f" =~ ^history/[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}/(Mon|Tue|Wed|Thu|Fri|Sat|Sun)/[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,90}\.json$ ]]; then
129:     FILE="$_f"
130:   else
131:     echo "publish_session: rejected file override: $_f" >&2
132:     exit 1
133:   fi
134: fi
135: 
136: # ── the layout: one flat pile sorted into folders ─────────────────────────
137: # Everything used to sit in the branch root, which made "what is this file and
138: # when is it from" a guessing game. Now: live/ for what is alive right now,
139: # models/ for the roster, snapshots/ for the audit/code pair, and history/ for
140: # everything historical, filed under the day and the weekday it belongs to.
141: #
142: # date_of_day <YYYYMMDD or YYYY-MM-DD> -> "YYYY-MM-DD/Tue"
143: history_bucket() {
144:   local raw="$1" d=""
145:   if [[ "$raw" =~ ^([0-9]{4})([0-9]{2})([0-9]{2})$ ]]; then
146:     d="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}-${BASH_REMATCH[2]}-${BASH_REMATCH[3]}"
147:   elif [[ "$raw" =~ ^([0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2})$ ]]; then
148:     d="$raw"
149:   else
150:     d="$(date -u '+%Y-%m-%d')"
151:   fi
152:   local wd
153:   wd="$(date -u -d "$d" '+%a' 2>/dev/null || true)"
154:   case "$wd" in
155:     Mon|Tue|Wed|Thu|Fri|Sat|Sun) : ;;
156:     *) wd="$(python3 -c "import datetime,sys;print(datetime.date.fromisoformat(sys.argv[1]).strftime('%a'))" "$d" 2>/dev/null || echo "")" ;;
157:   esac
158:   [ -n "$wd" ] || wd="---"
159:   printf '%s/%s' "$d" "$wd"
160: }
161: 
162: # A date out of a <name>-YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS.json stamp; today when there is none.
163: stamp_bucket() {
164:   local name="$1" raw=""
165:   if [[ "$name" =~ ([0-9]{8})T[0-9]{6} ]]; then raw="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"; fi
166:   history_bucket "$raw"
167: }

176:     models-*.json) printf 'models/%s' "$f"; return 0 ;;
177:     audit.json|code.json) printf 'snapshots/%s' "$f"; return 0 ;;
178:     handoff.json) printf 'live/handoff.json'; return 0 ;;

200: # every caller on the machine, and two publishes running at once overwrote each
201: # other's payload - caught by a local race test, where the Windows entry ended
202: # up carrying the Linux address. Staged under ~/.npm-hub/tmp, never /tmp.

205: if ! STAGE="$(TMPDIR="$HOME/.npm-hub/tmp" mktemp -t session.XXXXXX.json)"; then

207:   exit 1
208: fi
209: cleanup_publish() {
210:   cd / 2>/dev/null || true
211:   [ -n "$STAGE" ] && rm -f "$STAGE"
212:   [ -n "$WORK" ] && rm -rf "$WORK"
213: }
214: trap cleanup_publish EXIT

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Publish the live session's connection details so the panel can show them.
#
# The job summary already prints the address, user and password, but it is
# prose meant for a human with a browser: not machine-readable, and on a phone
# it is several taps behind the Actions UI. The panel is where the session is
# started, so it is where the credentials belong.
#
# They go to an orphan branch, session-state, as session.json. An orphan branch
# keeps this churn out of the history of main and lets the file be replaced
# wholesale every time without ever conflicting.
#
# WHO CAN READ THIS
#   On a public repository the branch is public, and so is the password in it.
#   That is the same exposure as the run summary, which is also public - but it
#   is worth being explicit, because a password on a web page feels different
#   from one in a log. Everything here dies with the runner within six hours,
#   and any secret in it is regenerated per run. If that is not acceptable,
#   make the repository private; the panel reads it with the same token either
#   way.
#
# TWO DESKS AT ONCE
#   Pass slot=linux, slot=windows or slot=agent and the entry lands in its own
#   file - session-linux.json, session-windows.json, session-agent.json,
#   session-opencode.json and session-hub.json - so
#   agent/opencode/hub take an -linux/-windows suffix (one file per OS, so two
#   runners stop overwriting each other); the bare slot stays for old runs.
#   the two desks and the agent never overwrite each other. Without a slot the
#   old single session.json is used, which keeps the older workflows working
#   unchanged.
#
#   The panel reads all three and shows whichever are live.
#
# MODELS AND SAVED SNAPSHOTS
#   Sessions alone do not survive usefully: which model answered, which died,
#   which recovered - that roster lives in ~/.zen_free_models.json on the
#   runner and dies with it. So every session also publishes its models:
#
#     publish_session.sh slot=agent file=models-agent.json \
#       kind=CLI-агент json=$HOME/.zen_free_models.json
#   file= overrides the target on the branch (validated: only the known
#   mailboxes are accepted, so a typo cannot spray files across the branch).
#   json= merges a local JSON file into the payload - with secrets scrubbed:
#   any key looking like a key/token/secret/password is dropped, because
#   opencode.json holds API keys and this branch may be public. Pass scrub=0
#   to disable.
#
# LAYOUT OF THE BRANCH (it used to be one pile in the root)
#   live/session-<slot>.json      the live descriptor, one per slot
#   live/handoff.json             the relay limits + the relay's live status
#   models/models-<slot>.json     the model roster of that session
#   snapshots/audit.json          the audit trail (was audit.json)
#   snapshots/code.json           the code snapshot (was code.json)
#   chats/<repo>.json             OpenCode chat bundles (unchanged)
#   history/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<Wd>/    everything historical, by day and weekday:
#       run-<runNumber>.json         one record per run: success or failure
#       saved-<slot>-<stamp>.json    the «Сохранить» snapshots
#       audit-<slot>-<stamp>.json
#       opencode-<stamp>.json
#   artifacts/<file>              files the user pushed from the hub
#   Every reader tries the new path first and falls back to the old root name,
#   so a branch that was never migrated keeps working.
#
#   publish_session.sh journal=1 writes the run record:
#     publish_session.sh journal=1 slot=hub-linux conclusion=success \
#       startedAt=... endedAt=...
#
# Usage: publish_session.sh key=value ...
#   Recognised keys are passed straight through to JSON, so a new session type
#   can add a field without touching this script.

set -uo pipefail

BRANCH="session-state"
FILE="live/session.json"
JOURNAL=0
# journal_date can come as an argument or from the environment; without it the
# record is filed under today (UTC).
JOURNAL_DATE="${JOURNAL_DATE:-}"

# A slot is a routing instruction, not data: pull it out of the arguments
# before they become JSON.
ARGS=()
JSON_FILES=()
FILE_OVERRIDE=""
SCRUB=1
EXPLICIT_STARTED_AT=0
for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    startedAt=*)   EXPLICIT_STARTED_AT=1; ARGS+=("$arg") ;;
    journal_date=*) JOURNAL_DATE="${arg#journal_date=}" ;;
    slot=linux)    FILE="live/session-linux.json" ;;
    slot=windows)  FILE="live/session-windows.json" ;;
    slot=agent)    FILE="live/session-agent.json" ;;
    slot=agent-linux)    FILE="live/session-agent-linux.json" ;;
    slot=agent-windows)  FILE="live/session-agent-windows.json" ;;
    slot=opencode) FILE="live/session-opencode.json" ;;
    slot=opencode-linux) FILE="live/session-opencode-linux.json" ;;
    slot=opencode-windows) FILE="live/session-opencode-windows.json" ;;
    slot=hub)      FILE="live/session-hub.json" ;;
    slot=hub-linux)      FILE="live/session-hub-linux.json" ;;
    slot=hub-windows)    FILE="live/session-hub-windows.json" ;;
    slot=phone)    FILE="live/session-phone.json" ;;
    slot=vnc)      FILE="live/session-vnc.json" ;;
    slot=*)        ;;   # unknown slot: ignore rather than write a stray file
    file=*)        FILE_OVERRIDE="$arg" ;;
    journal=1)     JOURNAL=1 ;;
    scrub=0)       SCRUB=0 ;;
    json=*)        # A Windows path (C:\Users\..) breaks mingw python; slashes

# the branch is a fixed set of mailboxes, not a scratch disk. The caller keeps
# using the old flat names; the layout below turns them into the new folders.

# ── the layout: one flat pile sorted into folders ─────────────────────────
# Everything used to sit in the branch root, which made "what is this file and
# when is it from" a guessing game. Now: live/ for what is alive right now,
# models/ for the roster, snapshots/ for the audit/code pair, and history/ for
# everything historical, filed under the day and the weekday it belongs to.
#
# date_of_day <YYYYMMDD or YYYY-MM-DD> -> "YYYY-MM-DD/Tue"
history_bucket() {
  local raw="$1" d=""

    *) wd="$(python3 -c "import datetime,sys;print(datetime.date.fromisoformat(sys.argv[1]).strftime('%a'))" "$d" 2>/dev/null || echo "")" ;;
  esac
  [ -n "$wd" ] || wd="---"
  printf '%s/%s' "$d" "$wd"
}

# A date out of a <name>-YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS.json stamp; today when there is none.
stamp_bucket() {
  local name="$1" raw=""
  if [[ "$name" =~ ([0-9]{8})T[0-9]{6} ]]; then raw="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"; fi
  history_bucket "$raw"
}

layout_file() {
  local f="$1" bucket
  case "$f" in
    live/*|chats/*|history/*|artifacts/*) printf '%s' "$f"; return 0 ;;
  esac
  case "$f" in
    session*.json) printf 'live/%s' "$f"; return 0 ;;
    models-*.json) printf 'models/%s' "$f"; return 0 ;;
    audit.json|code.json) printf 'snapshots/%s' "$f"; return 0 ;;
    handoff.json) printf 'live/handoff.json'; return 0 ;;
  esac
  if [[ "$f" == saved/* ]]; then
    # saved/audit-hub-20260102T030405.json -> history/2026-01-02/Fri/saved-audit-hub-...
    bucket="$(stamp_bucket "${f#saved/}")"
    printf 'history/%s/saved-%s' "$bucket" "${f#saved/}"
    return 0
  fi
  printf '%s' "$f"

export JSON_MERGE="$(printf '%s\n' "${JSON_FILES[@]}")"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# tmate rescue shell for a runner: a real SSH (and read-only web) session that
# survives the hub server, the cloudflared tunnel and even a wedged web app.
#
# WHY THIS EXISTS
#   The runner used to be unreachable the moment its web stack died. tmate
#   keeps a reverse session to the tmate hub: as long as the box itself is
#   alive, 'ssh <string>' from anywhere lands on the runner as the runner
#   user with full sudo - enough to inspect, run backup-work by hand, or save
#   whatever is worth keeping.
#
# WHAT IT DOES
#   1. installs tmate when missing (ubuntu-latest: plain apt, ~15s)
#   2. starts a detached tmate session on a fixed socket
#   3. publishes the connection strings to session-state control/rescue.json
#      (rewritten on beacons so the file going stale means the box is gone)
#   4. exits quietly without doing anything if installation fails - rescue
#      must never be the reason a session does not start
#
# ENV
#   GH_TOKEN / GITHUB_TOKEN   contents:write on the control repo
#   GITHUB_REPOSITORY         owner/repo
#   CONTROL_BRANCH            default session-state
#   RESCUE_BEACON_SEC         seconds between rescue.json beacons (default 60)
set -uo pipefail

HUB_LOGS="${HUB_LOGS:-$HOME/.npm-hub/logs}"
mkdir -p "$HUB_LOGS" 2>/dev/null || true
SOCK="$HUB_LOGS/tmate.sock"
VM="${CONTROL_TARGET:-hub}"
log() { echo "[rescue-ssh:$VM $(date -u '+%H:%M:%S')] $*" | tee -a "$HUB_LOGS/rescue-ssh-$VM.log"; }

TOKEN="${GH_TOKEN:-${GITHUB_TOKEN:-}}"
REPO="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:-sj0404-collab/zen-panel}"
BRANCH="${CONTROL_BRANCH:-session-state}"
BEACON="${RESCUE_BEACON_SEC:-60}"
API="https://api.github.com/repos/$REPO/contents"
RESCUE_PATH="control/rescue-$VM.json"

if ! command -v tmate >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "tmate missing - installing"
  if ! (sudo apt-get update -qq >/dev/null 2>&1 && sudo apt-get install -y -qq tmate >/dev/null 2>&1); then
    log "install failed; rescue ssh is OFF for this run"
    exit 0
  fi
fi

# One session per runner socket: reuse a live one instead of stacking new ones.
if ! tmate -S "$SOCK" ls >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  tmate -S "$SOCK" new-session -d 2>/dev/null || { log "new-session failed"; exit 0; }
fi

SSH=""; WEB=""
for i in $(seq 1 30); do
  SSH="$(tmate -S "$SOCK" display -p '#{tmate_ssh}' 2>/dev/null || true)"
  WEB="$(tmate -S "$SOCK" display -p '#{tmate_web_ro}' 2>/dev/null || true)"
  [ -n "$SSH" ] && break
  sleep 1
done
if [ -z "$SSH" ]; then
  log "tmate did not come up; rescue ssh is OFF"
  exit 0
fi

{
  echo ""
  echo "### Rescue shell (tmate)"
  echo ""
  echo "- ssh: \`$SSH\`"
  [ -n "$WEB" ] && echo "- read-only web: <${WEB}>"
  echo ""
} >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY" 2>/dev/null || true
log "up: $SSH"

publish() {
  local payload
  payload="$(python3 - "$@" <<'PY' 2>/dev/null || echo ""
import json, sys, datetime
print(json.dumps({
    "kind": "rescue-ssh",
    "vm": sys.argv[5],
    "state": sys.argv[1],
    "ssh": sys.argv[2],
    "web_ro": sys.argv[3],
    "runId": sys.argv[4],
    "beaconAt": datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"),
}, ensure_ascii=False))
PY
)"
  [ -n "$payload" ] || return 1
  [ -n "$TOKEN" ] || return 0
  local b64 sha
  b64="$(printf '%s' "$payload" | base64 -w0)"
  sha="$(curl -sf -m 20 -H "Authorization: token $TOKEN" "$API/control/rescue-$VM.json?ref=$BRANCH" 2>/dev/null \
      | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin).get("sha",""))' 2>/dev/null || echo)"
  if [ -n "$sha" ]; then
    curl -sf -m 20 -X PUT -H "Authorization: token $TOKEN" "$API/control/rescue-$VM.json" \
      -d "{\"message\":\"rescue beacon\",\"content\":\"$b64\",\"branch\":\"$BRANCH\",\"sha\":\"$sha\"}" >/dev/null
  else
    curl -sf -m 20 -X PUT -H "Authorization: token $TOKEN" "$API/control/rescue-$VM.json" \
      -d "{\"message\":\"rescue beacon\",\"content\":\"$b64\",\"branch\":\"$BRANCH\"}" >/dev/null
  fi
}

cleanup() {
  trap - TERM INT
  log "closing tmate"
  tmate -S "$SOCK" kill-session >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  publish ended "" "" "${GITHUB_RUN_ID:-local}" "$VM" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  exit 0
}
trap cleanup TERM INT

publish live "$SSH" "${WEB:-}" "${GITHUB_RUN_ID:-local}" "$VM" || log "publish failed (beacon will retry)"
while true; do
  sleep "$BEACON"
  if ! tmate -S "$SOCK" ls >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    log "tmate session died - relaunching"
    tmate -S "$SOCK" new-session -d 2>/dev/null || continue
    for i in $(seq 1 30); do
      SSH="$(tmate -S "$SOCK" display -p '#{tmate_ssh}' 2>/dev/null || true)"
      [ -n "$SSH" ] && break
      sleep 1
    done
  fi
  publish live "${SSH:-}" "${WEB:-}" "${GITHUB_RUN_ID:-local}" "$VM" || true
done

name: NPM Hub

# The third agent: npm-hub on a runner, in a browser tab of the panel.
#
# WHAT IT IS
#   npm-hub/ is a tools dashboard with xterm terminal tabs: it detects the
#   installed AI CLI agents (claude, gemini, codex, copilot, opencode and
#   friends) and opens each in its own terminal session, with a file manager
#   and a live model registry on top. All of that logic already lives in the
#   repo - this workflow optionally preinstalls the CLIs, starts the server and
#   publishes the address, the same way the desks and the other agents do.
#
#   No work branch, no autosave: the hub edits nothing by itself, it is a
#   launcher. What outlives the runner is the models snapshot
#   (models-hub-<os>.json, one per OS) and whatever the user saves through the panel.
#
# AUTH
#   Panel-launched runs carry a gate token (the `token` input, generated per
#   launch): without ?zt= the hub answers 401 on every page, API call and
#   terminal socket. The tunnel address itself stays unguessable and dies
#   with the run (six hours at most).

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      os:
        description: "Runner OS"
        type: choice
        options: [linux, windows]
        default: linux
      label:
        description: "Name for this session"
        type: string
        default: "hub"
      token:
        description: "Hub gate token, generated by the panel (empty = no gate)"
        type: string
        default: ""
      gh_token:
        description: "GitHub PAT for the server-side /gh proxy (empty = proxy off)"
        type: string
        default: ""
      runner_linux:
        description: "Runner for the Linux job (a label, or self-hosted - see pc-local/runner)"
        type: string
        default: "ubuntu-latest"
      runner_windows:
        description: "Runner for the Windows job (a label, or self-hosted - see pc-local/runner)"
        type: string
        default: "windows-latest"
      preinstall:
        description: "Install all CLI agents at startup (minutes); off = each installs at first click"
        type: boolean
        default: false
      replace:
        description: "Replace an active session run"
        type: boolean
        default: false
      handoff:
        description: "This run takes over a session that another runner handed over"
        type: boolean
        default: false
      handoff_from:
        description: "runId of the runner that handed the session over"
        type: string
        default: ""
      rescue_ssh:
        description: "tmate rescue shell published to session-state control/rescue.json (lifeline when the hub+web die)"
        type: boolean
        default: true
      command_queue:
        description: "safe command queue on session-state control/queue.json (whitelisted ops only)"
        type: boolean
        default: true

concurrency:
  group: zen-panel-session-${{ github.repository }}
  # A handoff run must NOT cancel the runner it takes over from: that runner
  # saves, waits until this one has published itself, and only then steps aside.
  # A manual «заменить» from the panel still cancels the old run.
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ inputs.replace && !inputs.handoff }}

permissions:
  contents: write

env:
  HUB_LOGS: /home/runner/.npm-hub/logs

jobs:
  # ── Hub on Linux ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
  hub:
    if: inputs.os == 'linux'
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner_linux }}
    timeout-minutes: 360

          key: hub-pkg-linux-${{ github.run_id }}
          restore-keys: hub-pkg-linux-

      - name: Install the CLI agents

mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STATE_DIR")"
          rm -rf "$STATE_DIR"
          STATE_REMOTE="https://x-access-token:${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}@github.com/${{ github.repository }}.git"
          if ! git clone -q --depth 1 --filter=blob:limit=1m --branch session-state \
               "$STATE_REMOTE" "$STATE_DIR" 2>/dev/null; then
            if ! git clone -q --depth 1 --branch session-state \
                 "$STATE_REMOTE" "$STATE_DIR" 2>/dev/null; then
              STATE_DIR=""
              echo "::notice::no session-state branch yet; starting without the saved history"
            fi
          fi
          # Restore repos before importing OpenCode sessions: opencode import
          # needs the real repository CWD, not an empty placeholder folder.
          # The fork's own history does not depend on that restore, so the two
          # run together; the hub-work chats import below waits for the repos,
          # and runs after the fork restore so the two never copy the same
          # opencode bundle at the same time.
          # Repo restore is opt-in from the hub's Snapshot tab now: pulling the
          # whole work-backup copy BEFORE the tunnel publishes cost the connect
          # page ~4 of the user's minutes at every launch. The script sees
          # WORK_BACKUP_RESTORE=0 and exits at once; everything else in this
          # step (audit/code, chat bundles) is small and stays.
          GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" WORK_BACKUP_ROOT="$HOME" \
            WORK_BACKUP_RESTORE=0 WORK_BACKUP_RESTORE_EXISTING=1 bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/restore-work.sh" \
            2>&1 | tee -a "$HUB_LOGS/restore-work.log" &
          WORK_PID=$!
